**What type of PR is this?**
/kind bug

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
Fixes #87898 by passing Context to tryAcquireOrRenew so that the duration of timeoutCtx is respected.
The reported race condition is resolved since there is no additional goroutine involved.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
Fixes #87898

```release-note
NONE
```

Would it work to refactor this:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/64ba0bf3d6630c3565e2886d0ab923fac4ac2a66/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/leaderelection/leaderelection.go#L266-L277

So that we don't need a go routine? E.g. pass timeoutCtx to tryAcquireOrRenew.

Looking at tryAcquireOrRenew and its caller, the timeoutCtx is used by the caller to bound the total time the operation takes.
Using goroutine is standard practice in this use case.

Sure, I'm suggesting that we move it deeper, either into tryAcquireOrRenew or into lock implementations. The problem is that the go routine wraps a bunch of stuff that it doesn't need to. We really only care about timing out this:

https://github.com/tedyu/kubernetes/blob/087fc126b46f2c225aa74e88d0153dc4763ba443/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/leaderelection/leaderelection.go#L375

Yes, I think refactoring the leaderelection code to make it ~single-threaded would be better. There is at least one obvious race remaining that this doesn't catch (namely, the race between cml.Get and cml.Update that spawned the original report in #87800), and there are quite likely others.

It's always better to eliminate potential concurrency problems by the simple expedient of not having any data shared between goroutines :)

I have started the refactoring.
Currently trying to get over compilation errors such as:
```
resourcelock/interface.go:127:3: cannot use leaseLock (type *LeaseLock) as type Interface in return argument:
	*LeaseLock does not implement Interface (wrong type for Update method)
		have Update(context.Context, LeaderElectionRecord) error
		want Update(LeaderElectionRecord) error
```
After https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/87299 goes in, you can pass a context directly to the client call.

Good to know.
The following refactoring is still needed:
```
func (ll *LeaseLock) Update(ctx context.Context, ler LeaderElectionRecord) error {
```

> Good to know.
> The following refactoring is still needed:
> 
> ```
> func (ll *LeaseLock) Update(ctx context.Context, ler LeaderElectionRecord) error {
> ```

Yes, there are multiple implementations of resource lock, and they will all need to take a Context. Fortunately it's only about a three-word change for each.
/priority important-soon

As @mikedanese pointed out, after #87299 goes in, you won't have to switch to the untyped client interfaces to plumb Contexts through. Also since I believe #87299 is already breaking client-go compatibility you won't need to fork out a separate UpdateWithCtx method in LeaseInterface.

I have removed UpdateWithCtx from LeaseInterface.

Just wanted to get a compilable version which @howardjohn can validate.

@jktomer @mikedanese 
Please review.
I have confirmed this fixes the initial issue I reported. 1000+ tests run with no race

review_comments: I think we need to pass the context down to resourcelock.Interface.Get() as well as Update() or risk changing the timeout behavior of this code. @mikedanese you can probably figure out easier than I can whether the difference is significant (i.e. is there any time bound on client requests if no context is passed in?)

There's a default timeout on the client that is probably not set. I think the timeout behavior change here is desirable. There's also server side timeout enforcement that gets applied to these requests.
